quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Car drivers should know that large trucks:

options.text: Have large blind spots.
Can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.
Do not need more room to maneuver than passenger vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have large blind spots.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have large blind spots in front, on the sides, and in the rear. Do not stay in these areas. Trucks need more room to turn and stop than passenger vehicles because of their size and weight.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Sharp turn to the right.
Double curve.
Winding road.
Pavement ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead has a series of turns and curves.

questions.question: You may cross solid yellow lines:

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
During daylight hours only.
At any time.
When making turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making turns.
questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed, but solid lines cannot. The only time you can cross a solid yellow line is when you are turning.

questions.question: When driving near a blind pedestrian who is carrying a white cane or using a guide dog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and be prepared to stop.
Take the right-of-way.
Proceed normally.
Drive away quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be prepared to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and give them the right-of-way. Be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: A good rule to remember for passing is:

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only as needed.
Try to get to the front of any slow-moving traffic so that you can see better.
Always flash your lights and sound your horn to alert other drivers to your intentions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only as needed.
questions.explanation: Every time you pass another vehicle, the risk of a crash increases. If you drive faster than other vehicles, you will need to keep passing them. Instead, drive with traffic at the legal speed limit and pass only when necessary.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: When pavement is wet, reduce your speed.
The road ahead winds a series of turns or curves.
Traffic increases ahead.
Steep grade ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pavement is wet, reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet. In wet conditions, slow down, avoid sudden braking or sharp turns, and keep more distance between your vehicle and the one in front.

questions.question: On long trips, you can prevent drowsiness by:

options.text: Turning on your car radio.
Slowing down.
Stopping at regular intervals for a rest.
Moving your eyes from side to side as you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping at regular intervals for a rest.
questions.explanation: Stop regularly on long trips to rest and stretch. Do this even if you do not feel tired.

questions.question: The posted speed limit shows:

options.text: Only a recommended driving speed.
The exact speed at which you must travel to avoid a ticket.
The maximum safe driving speed under ideal road and weather conditions.
The maximum safe driving speed under all road conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe driving speed under ideal road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit sign shows the highest legal speed for that road. You may need to drive slower than the limit. When road or weather conditions are poor, you should drive more slowly.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true?

options.text: It is okay for drivers of other vehicles to follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle with two people on it is more balanced than a motorcycle with just one rider.
The driver of a passenger vehicle must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.
Drivers of other vehicles can expect a motorcycle's brake lights to turn on when the motorcyclist slows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver of a passenger vehicle must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use the full width of a lane. When passing a motorcycle on the left, move completely into the left lane before passing.

questions.question: When you see this black and yellow sign, it means:

options.text: The road to the right is for one-way traffic only.
That due to upcoming roadwork, there is a detour to the right.
Slow down because the road ahead changes direction at an extreme angle.
There is a crossroad to your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down because the road ahead changes direction at an extreme angle.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road ahead turns sharply at an extreme angle. Slow down before you reach this sharp curve, just as you would at a sharp intersection turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is coming.
Look both ways before you cross the intersection.
Always come to a complete stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. You must stop completely if traffic requires it.

questions.question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, you:

options.text: Can still turn, but you must let oncoming traffic go first.
Cannot turn anymore and must go straight.
Still have the right to turn.
No longer need to turn in the direction the arrow showed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can still turn, but you must let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you can still turn the direction the arrow pointed. But first, you must let pedestrians and oncoming traffic pass.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light works the same as:

options.text: A slow sign.
A yield sign.
A stop sign.
An intersection sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign.
questions.explanation: At a flashing red light, you must stop and let all other traffic pass before you go.

questions.question: When can you drive in a lane showing a red X?

options.text: If there is no oncoming traffic.
If you are passing the car ahead.
Between sunset and sunrise.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Lane signs with a red X show which lanes are closed. Never drive in a lane with a red X.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, turn your steering wheel:

options.text: To keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the car to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the car to go.
questions.explanation: When your car skids, turn the wheel in the direction you want it to go. Once the car straightens out, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: When turning left, you must let these people go first:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.
Oncoming traffic.
Pedestrians already in the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When turning left, always let oncoming traffic, pedestrians, and other drivers in the intersection go first.

questions.question: You can pass another vehicle if the line between lanes is a ____ line.

options.text: Broken white
Double solid yellow
Solid yellow
Solid white

questions.correctAnswerText: Broken white
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if the lane ahead is clear.

questions.question: You see a flashing yellow light at an intersection. You should:

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Drive slowly and carefully through the intersection.
Get ready to stop because the light is turning red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly and carefully through the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means go through the intersection slowly and with care. Look both ways for traffic.

questions.question: Which one does NOT affect how far it takes to stop your car?

options.text: Steering ability
Braking distance
Reaction distance
Perception time

questions.correctAnswerText: Steering ability
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change with your speed and road conditions.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It helps skills but hurts judgment.
It hurts both skills and judgment.
It does not affect either skills or judgment.
It does not affect judgment but hurts skills.

questions.correctAnswerText: It hurts both skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms skills needed for safe driving, like reaction time and clear vision. It also hurts your judgment about speed and distance, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly when they are:

options.text: Flat.
Curvy.
In the sun.
Shaded.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shaded.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas freeze faster than other parts of the road. Trees and buildings block the sun. These areas also dry last. Be extra careful in these spots when it is cold or wet.

questions.question: Work zone signs mean:

options.text: It is summer.
You must immediately stop and back up.
Driving conditions are not ideal.
You should drive faster to get out of the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are not ideal.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange. They warn you that work is happening on or near the road. Drive slowly and carefully when you see these signs.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway. You see children playing nearby. Before you start to move your car, you should:

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children that you are moving.
Sound your horn so the children will hear you.
Walk to the back of the car to be sure the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of the car to be sure the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Get out and check behind your car before backing up. Do not rely only on your mirrors. This is especially important when children are nearby. They are small and hard to see.

questions.question: You are driving when it begins to rain. You should:

options.text: Drive faster than surrounding traffic.
Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.
Slow down.
Drive closely behind the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When it rains, slow down. Turn on your headlights so others can see you. If rain is very heavy and you cannot see well, drive to the shoulder and stop until it clears.

questions.question: Before switching on the ignition, you should:

options.text: Be sure only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Be sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Be sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Be sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Make it a habit to buckle your seat belt before you start the car. Make sure everyone in the car does the same.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
U-turns are prohibited.
You may proceed if the way is clear.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: If you see this sign, you are going the wrong way. You could have a head-on crash. Turn around carefully.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Crossroad ahead.
Flagger ahead.
Lane ends.
Turn right or go straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about upcoming road hazards. This sign warns you that a crossroad is coming.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, entering or leaving a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. This tells other drivers what you plan to do and helps prevent accidents.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at the same time to an open intersection:

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver may continue driving without stopping.
One driver should honk to indicate that they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: If you arrive at an open intersection at the same time as another car, yield to the car on your right. Wait until it is safe, then proceed.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle stopped on the side of the road, drivers should:

options.text: Increase their speed.
Move to the lane farthest from the stopped vehicle or slow down.
Pull off the road behind the stationary vehicle.
Move to the lane closest to the stationary vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the lane farthest from the stopped vehicle or slow down.
questions.explanation: The Move Over Law protects police, firefighters, tow truck drivers, and utility workers stopped on the roadside. You must move away from their lane if you can do so safely. If you cannot move over, slow down to at least 20 mph below the speed limit.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Slam on your brakes.
Hold the steering wheel tightly and slow down to a stop.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on your emergency flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tightly and slow down to a stop.
questions.explanation: Do not brake suddenly if your tire blows out. Grip the steering wheel firmly to stay in your lane. Let off the gas and slow down gradually. Once you are going very slowly, apply the brakes gently and move to the side of the road.

questions.question: You are driving very slowly and cars are backing up behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Drive even slower.
Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
Do not let other cars pass you.
Use your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is dangerous. If you are on a two-lane road and cars are backing up behind you, pull off the road to let them pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curves ahead.
Divided highway starts.
Divided highway ends.
Bumps in the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the divided highway is ending ahead.

questions.question: After how many drinks does your crash risk increase?

options.text: Four drinks.
Three drinks.
Two drinks.
One drink.

questions.correctAnswerText: One drink.
questions.explanation: Even one drink increases your crash risk compared to not drinking at all. No amount of alcohol is safe when driving, no matter how experienced you are.

questions.question: Is night driving more or less dangerous than day driving?

options.text: Less dangerous.
The same.
More dangerous.
Easier on your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous than day driving. It is harder to see, headlights can blind you, and more tired or impaired drivers are on the road.

questions.question: When you see this sign, what must you do?

options.text: Stop completely and look for pedestrians and cross traffic.
Slow down without stopping completely.
Stop completely and wait for a green light.
Slow down and check for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and look for pedestrians and cross traffic.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign is a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop and check for pedestrians and other vehicles crossing the intersection. Wait until it is clear before you proceed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Keep right.
Low shoulder.
No parking at any time.
Lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This regulation sign tells drivers to stay on the right side to avoid a hazard ahead.

questions.question: What should you do when a school bus stops with its stop arm extended?

options.text: Stop completely and wait to proceed.
Honk and pass the bus on the left.
Keep driving when you think children are done exiting.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and wait to proceed.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has its stop arm out, you must come to a complete stop. Do not move until the stop arm goes back in.

questions.question: What should you do if your tire blows out?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not use your brakes right away.
Gradually slow down and pull off the road.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If your tire blows out, release the gas pedal and avoid using the brakes immediately. Gradually slow down and gently apply the brakes as you move to the side of the road.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong coffee to stay awake.
They may drive as poorly as a drunk driver.
They can stay alert by opening a window and playing loud music.
They are usually older drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may drive as poorly as a drunk driver.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive as poorly as drunk drivers. Opening windows, playing loud music, or drinking coffee does not make a tired driver alert enough to drive safely.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow traffic light?

options.text: Speed up to get through before it turns red.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Watch what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means red is coming next. Stop unless you are already inside the intersection.

questions.question: Which statement about emergency vehicles is true?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and flashing lights.
They can use a loudspeaker to give instructions.
They can follow each other.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles pass. They have the right-of-way when using sirens or lights. Follow their loudspeaker instructions. They often follow each other, so wait until it is clear before moving.

questions.question: When driving where children are playing, what should you expect?

options.text: They will know when it is safe to cross the street.
They will stop at the curb before crossing.
They will run into the street without looking.
They will not cross unless with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: They will run into the street without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful around children. They may not understand danger and could run into the street without looking.

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?

options.text: Before you start your engine.
While backing out of your driveway.
When you reach 55 mph.
When you finish a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start your engine.
questions.explanation: Before you start driving, adjust all mirrors so you can see without leaning forward or backward.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
It does not matter which lights you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: What should you do if traffic lights at an intersection are not working?

options.text: Park off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to show other drivers what you plan to do.
Turn on hazard lights and go through without stopping.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When traffic lights are not working, treat the intersection as a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers the same way you would at a four-way stop, then go through carefully when it is your turn.

questions.question: What affects how much space you need to cross traffic?

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
Whether there is a stop sign.
Whether you use your turn signals.
The cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Guide signs have a ____ background and show directions and distances.

options.text: Yellow
Red
Green
White

questions.correctAnswerText: Green
questions.explanation: Guide signs have a green background and show directions and distances to places. They help you find your way when driving in unfamiliar areas.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Stop where you are.
Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights behind you, pull over safely to the right side and stop. In heavy traffic, move slowly until you can get out of the way.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Slam on your brakes to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down to let them pass.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check for tailgaters often. If someone is following too close, slow down and let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen when drivers follow too closely.
